text:
alex: Heads-up: brought up ganymede-int6-v1 (quant int6) for summarization benchmark. Observed lower p95 latency but a small quality drop on long docs and some coldstart OOMs on older hosts. Anyone else seeing fragmentation?

maria: saw the same on a couple canaries. p95 down ~22% but rougeL -1.8 pts on news longform set. OOMs when max_new_tokens >= 512.

raj: logs show KV alloc spikes, fragmentation pattern matches earlier int4 coldstarts. Worker pages show many small free blocks. suspect allocator vs int6 packing.

eval-bot: eval results: model=ganymede-int6-v1, dataset=summ-long-100, rougeL: baseline=43.7 -> 42.0, bertscore:F1 0.89->0.875, latency p95 240ms->185ms.

alex: proposed quick mitigation: reduce default max_new_tokens for summarize route to 256 for this variant and enforce prefetch=false on coldstart. Canary config below.

alex: ```
route: summarize
model_variant: ganymede-int6-v1
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  batch_size: 8
  prefetch: false
  warmup: 2
```

lucy: also suggest enabling KV trim threshold during idle to reduce fragmentation: set kv_trim_on_alloc_failure: true and kv_trim_threshold: 0.65

owen: would prefer to test microbatch pacing: max_concurrent_batches=2, pacing_ms=10. reduces mem spikes.

sam: for quality regression we should run focused eval: long-doc prompt amplifiers and hallucination checks. Maybe apply 1% rerank via v2 to detect regressions.

maria: agree. Also run a quick quant-sanity check: compare int8 vs int6 topk distributions for logits on 100 samples.

raj: I'll instrument alloc histograms and attach flame graph later. For now rolling canary with alex's defaults to 10% traffic.

deploy-bot: started canary deploy ganymede-int6-v1 -> 10% on summarize route

alex: thanks. tag me if OOMs spike. If no increase in hallucinations after 24h we can consider bumping max_new_tokens back to 384.

eval-bot: note: scheduled eval job 'summ-long-regress-check' queued, ETA 45m.
